exposure: Body mass index (BMI) in women aged ≥35 years
BMI categories in women aged ≥35 years
cohort: 912 Polish women with singleton pregnancies, recruited in 2015-2016
finding: Older maternal age was associated with an increased risk of various obstetric complications, including preeclampsia, gestational hypertension, gestational diabetes, cesarean section, preterm birth, low birth weight, and macrosomia, with the risk further amplified by obesity, particularly in women aged 35 years and older.
mod_finding: Older age was associated with a higher chance of cesarean section.
